author: Juravieal
title: How the power rankings work, and where league games fit
summary: A question came up about whether the power rankings count the cross-conference league games. Short answer: the ranking doesn't use anyone's wins or losses, but two of its columns leave league games out, and that should change.

ol: Each week, every team plays everybody. Your score is compared with all 19 other teams' scores in both conferences. Beat 14 of them and you go 14-5 for that week. This is called an all-play record.
Add the weeks up. After 7 weeks everyone has played 133 of these virtual games.
Sort by all-play win percentage. If two teams tie, the one with more points per game ranks higher.

blocks.p: That's the whole ranking. Who you happened to play doesn't matter, only how many points you scored. It answers "who is actually good?" rather than "who has won?"

ul: The ranking: a league game is just one more opponent. Your score that week is already compared with all 19 teams, including your league-game opponent, so it can't add anything new. Your score counts once per week, the same way the league table counts points for.
The Record column: it shows the Sleeper conference record only, so league-game wins and losses are missing. Juravieal shows 5-2 there but is really 7-3.
Luck: actual wins minus the wins your scores deserved. It also counts conference wins only.

blocks.p: The League table on the Conferences tab is the one that counts league games, and it already does: all 20 teams by total wins, then points for.

ArmedRodgery21 is 10-0 and top of the league table but #2 in power, because Argrider scores about 7.5 more a week (153.1 against 145.6). seachicken22 is 6-4 but #14 in power: below-average scores and some luck. A good record and a strong team aren't the same thing.

proposal.question: Show the full league record on the Power tab, and count league games in Luck?
proposal.detail: The ranking itself stays the same. Only the Record and Luck columns change.
